title: bitwidth-lift-sensitivity-workbook
content:
Purpose:
This workbook is a lightweight, experiment-first spreadsheet blueprint for estimating the net economics of moving a serving workload from (baseline) FP16/FP32 to INT8 / FP8 / 4-bit (and hybrid mixes). The goal is to produce a small matrix you can populate from microbenchmarks and an A/B rollout to give a recommendation with explicit risk tolerances (quality delta thresholds and latency SLOs).

How to use this file: quick steps
- Run the microbench harness for your target model and representative prompt length distribution (prompt/tokens/sample lengths). Capture throughput and p50/p95 generation latency for baseline (FP16) then for each quant profile (INT8, FP8, 4-bit, hybrid).
- Populate the scenario table below and then use the heuristics section to synthesize an initial recommendation.
- If quality delta > threshold, run a small canary (1–5% traffic) with offline eval prompts and live QA/LLM eval monitoring.

Minimum columns for the spreadsheet (copy to your sheet):
- scenario_id (string)
- model (string) e.g. redwood-7b-v2
- quant_profile (string) e.g. fp16, int8, fp8, 4bit, hybrid-kv-int8
- quant_lib (string) e.g. bitsandbytes-0.42, custom-fp8-kernel-v1
- eval_dataset (string) e.g. truthset-chat-1k
- eval_metric (string) e.g. qa-f1, ppl, rouge)
- baseline_throughput_tps (number, tokens/sec)
- baseline_latency_p50_ms
- quant_throughput_tps
- quant_latency_p50_ms
- cost_per_million_tokens_baseline_usd
- cost_per_million_tokens_quant_usd
- quality_delta_pct (quant vs baseline on chosen metric; positive = improvement)
- notes (string)

Example spreadsheet row (text form):
- scenario_id: s-20250214-1
- model: redwood-13b-v1
- quant_profile: int8
- quant_lib: bnb-0.39
- eval_dataset: conv-eval-5k
- eval_metric: qa-f1
- baseline_throughput_tps: 1200
- baseline_latency_p50_ms: 85
- quant_throughput_tps: 1650
- quant_latency_p50_ms: 72
- cost_per_million_tokens_baseline_usd: 60.00
- cost_per_million_tokens_quant_usd: 39.00
- quality_delta_pct: -0.6
- notes: "INT8 improved throughput and lowered cost; tiny F1 drop; KV cache behavior unchanged."

Baseline economics assumptions (example model of unit costs):
- We treat cost_per_million_tokens as the sum of amortized GPU runtime, memory-resident cache, and infra overhead. Baseline FP16 number is example only.
- Example baseline (FP16): $60 / 1e6 tokens (this is a working-number; replace with your infra measured value).
- Multipliers observed in our org (approx):
  - INT8: runtime cost multiplier ~ 0.65x (35% cost reduction), latency multiplier 0.9–1.0x depending on kernel maturity, quality delta typically small (-0.5% to -1.5% on sensitive metrics).
  - FP8: runtime cost multiplier ~ 0.75x, latency multiplier ~0.85–0.95x, quality delta moderate (-0.5% to -3%).
  - 4-bit (symmetric quant / group-wise): runtime cost multiplier ~ 0.40x–0.60x, latency multiplier ~0.7–0.9x, quality delta variable (-2% to -10% depending on model and task).

Simple cost math to add into sheet (cell formulas you can paste):
- cost_savings_pct = 1 - (cost_per_million_tokens_quant_usd / cost_per_million_tokens_baseline_usd)
- tokens_per_dollar_baseline = 1_000_000 / cost_per_million_tokens_baseline_usd
- tokens_per_dollar_quant = 1_000_000 / cost_per_million_tokens_quant_usd
- expected_daily_savings_usd = daily_tokens_consumed / 1_000_000 * (cost_baseline - cost_quant)
- breakeven_infra_effort_days = (estimated_engineering_days * daily_savings_usd) ? (This is a placeholder — capture eng effort separately.)

Quality vs cost decision thresholds (proposal):
- For high-safety workloads (billing, legal summarization, regulatory): require quality_delta_pct >= -0.5% to consider non-FP16.
- For user-facing prose (chat, assistant): accept up to -1.5% if latency gains >= 10% or cost savings >= 30%.
- For background batch embeddings/analytics: accept -5% or more if cost reduction > 50%.
- Always prefer hybrid approaches (cache + mixed precision) when quality is near threshold.

Heuristics / recommended quant strategies by workload pattern:
- Short-turn chat (prompt + <128 tokens): latency is king. Prefer FP8 or INT8 when kernels reduce p50 by >= 8% and quality delta within threshold. 4-bit may hurt fluency.
- Long generations (>512 tokens): throughput dominates; 4-bit or aggressive mixed schemes can be attractive if QA metrics on long-form retrieval tasks remain acceptable.
- Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): quantize the model but keep vector index storage unchanged; or use hybrid: KV-cache in fp16, activations quantized for generation path. This preserves prefix fidelity.
- Heavy caching workloads (high cache-hit rate): quantization benefits shrink because compute proportional share decreases. Recompute effective savings: effective_cost_reduction = cost_reduction * (1 - cache_hit_rate).

Quick formula for cache-aware savings (to copy into the sheet):
- effective_cost_quant = baseline_cost * (cache_hit_rate) + quant_cost * (1 - cache_hit_rate)
- effective_savings_pct = 1 - (effective_cost_quant / baseline_cost)

Experiment checklist (what to capture during each run):
- exact model binary and seed used, quantization toolchain and parameters (per-channel, symmetric/asymmetric, group size), kernel version, GPU type and driver.
- prompt length distribution and representative live traces (attach sample of 1000 prompts).
- microbench harness results: tokens/sec steady-state, p50/p95 latency, CUDA utilization, GPU memory footprint, temperature.
- evaluation: run the curated eval set and a 1k live-traffic holdout for true online signal.
- cost model inputs: instance-hour, amortized GPU cost, infra overhead, multi-tenant discounting.

Decision rubric (automatable):
- If quality_delta_pct >= -1% and cost_savings_pct >= 30% -> recommend canary (5% traffic for 72 hours) with auto-rollback on metric drift > 1% absolute or latency SLO violation.
- If quality_delta_pct in (-3%, -1%] and cost_savings_pct >= 50% -> recommend multi-stage rollout with A/B tests and human eval on samples.
- If quality_delta_pct <= -3% -> do NOT recommend full rollout; investigate hybrid-mix or improved kernels.

Short worked example (scenario):
- Baseline: FP16 cost = $60 / 1e6 tokens; p50 = 85ms; tps = 1200.
- INT8 measured: cost = $39 / 1e6 tokens; p50 = 72ms; tps = 1650; quality_delta = -0.6% on QA-F1.
- FP8 measured: cost = $45 / 1e6 tokens; p50 = 68ms; tps = 1780; quality_delta = -1.0%
- 4-bit measured: cost = $26 / 1e6 tokens; p50 = 60ms; tps = 2400; quality_delta = -6.8%
- Cache hit rate = 25% for this workload.
- effective INT8 cost = 60*0.25 + 39*0.75 = $46.75 -> net savings ~ 22.1% (not 35% because of cache)
- conclusion: because effective_savings_pct < 30% and quality_delta ~ -0.6% we recommend a small canary for INT8 rather than full rollout; 4-bit is only candidate for non-critical batch jobs.

Unresolved questions / open experiments (items to add to sprint backlog):
- Kernel-level FP8 runtimes: test on A100 vs H100 for latency parity.
- Per-token quality drift patterns (does 4-bit harm early tokens more than later ones?) Capture token-level log-prob deltas.
- Mixed-precision strategies for KV-caching: formalize hybrid recipes (cache: fp16, compute: 4-bit) and measure memory vs perf tradeoffs.
- Automated heuristics in the Console: add a "quant recommendation" card that feeds from this workbook for customer-specific runbooks.

Quick rollout checklist (for SRE/Console teams):
- gating KPIs: eval_metric (chosen), p50 latency, p95 latency, error-rate increase, cost per million tokens, rollback conditions pre-defined.
- allocate 2 reserved nodes for canary to isolate noise.
- autoscaling policy: ensure scale-up thresholds unaffected by kernel jitter.

Notes_to_self (informal):
- Capture kernel versions in the infra tags (driver, libcudnn, NCCL) — tiny driver differences can flip 4-bit latency regressions.
- Ask solutions-eng to produce a short customer one-pager for customers who ask for 50% cost cuts vs 2% QA regression.
- Add an example dashboard in Console that overlays cost, latency, and quality deltas over a 14-day window.

Appendix: suggested short-run experiments (priority order)
1) Run baseline + INT8 + INT8 with per-channel optimizations on 1 model and one eval set.
2) Run FP8 kernels if available, compare p50/p95 and mem usage.
3) Run 4-bit in a batch job only, measure token-level perplexity drift.
4) Run hybrid (cache fp16 + generate 4-bit) and measure effective_savings with a real cache-hit trace.
